scope: Independent contract-only review against cited local files. Reviewer did not author this contract. No source or contract edited; saved-source analysis is not a policy handoff or native runtime reader.
conclusion: No concrete contradiction found. Narrow source-interval provenance, incomplete-exclusion refusal, per-interval page containment, revision-specific BootArgs handling and external final-tree hashing are sound directions. Native policy/handoff completeness remains unproved.

checks.point: Known non-overlap is not exhaustive reservation discovery
checks.assessment: The contract limits its positive result to recorded MCC, framebuffer, pmap-io and device-segment data. It explicitly keeps omitted/unknown classes and source coverage as a handoff blocker. Source range checks and current zero intersections do not establish a complete exclusion inventory.

evidence.source_fact: Actual DRAM information is distinct from kernel-managed memory bounds.
pa_valid checks only the managed interval.
Physical-hole handling is explicitly a TODO; pmap_valid_page delegates to the interval check.
pmap-io records include physical/decorating flags; they are not a guarantee that every platform reservation is inventoried.

checks.point: Guest envelope remains one original source interval, not all DRAM
checks.assessment: The proposed candidate is the single source-derived guest managed interval with preserved original upper bound. The contract forbids widening or merging it with neighboring RAM. It correctly says the present launcher did not compute a new complete carveout-derived cap.

evidence.source_fact: Pinned loader preserves the original managed upper bound while changing the guest base and recomputing size.
Those derived values populate guest initial BootArgs fields.
Kernel takes management base/size from BootArgs and may reduce the size further.
Wrapper checks the payload reservation against recorded carveouts; this is not a whole-DRAM completeness producer.

checks.limit: Full guest BootArgs bytes were not separately captured. Saved-envelope corroboration is a source-bound derivation from original bytes, recorded layout and matching frozen loader, not a new runtime read.

checks.point: A page cannot cross two adjacent original RAM intervals
checks.assessment: The contract explicitly preserves original RAM boundaries and requires the entire page within one interval. Exact union is allowed for reservation coverage only; it does not permit merging RAM intervals to admit a cross-boundary page.

evidence.source_fact: span_valid accepts RAM membership only if one individual source range contains the entire page; adjacent ranges are not combined.

checks.future_test_required: Synthetic adjacent intervals and a straddling page must refuse; no policy helper was implemented or tested here.

checks.point: Empty/partial carveout data does not prove no reservations
checks.assessment: The contract requires slot validation/coverage or an equivalently trusted complete scoped source, not merely a well-formed sentinel list. It rejects missing required encodings and partial records. The saved list alone cannot establish the classification of every source slot.

evidence.source_fact: Selected source profile has four TZ slots.
List construction assumes common plane configuration and has a profile-absent fallback, not a universal device-reservation census.
An enabled slot with bad bounds is warned about and skipped, so a bounded list may omit an invalid enabled slot.
Upstream parses the property by integer division; that does not validate absence of partial trailing data.
Current bounded capture validates list shape/ranges/sentinel, not all omitted slot status or global exclusion coverage.

checks.point: Captured BootArgs writer differs from native header layout
checks.assessment: Confirmed: captured revision uses a608-byte command line and the saved blob is736 bytes; pinned native header unconditionally declares a1024-byte command line. Common initial envelope fields are source-aligned, but the tail cannot be read through sizeof(native boot_args) as this capture. The contract explicitly forbids that and leaves per-revision tail/native layout implementation unproved.

evidence.source_fact: Revision-specific writer declares the shorter command-line capacity and its tail fields.
Writer selection uses the actual BootArgs revision.
Native command-line capacity is unconditionally1024.
Native tail follows its longer CommandLine field.
PE_state stores the supplied BootArgs pointer; it does not prove that a mismatched native struct tail became valid.

checks.limit: No native offsetof/sizeof compile or runtime reader was performed. Any future reader still needs its own exact layout validation.

checks.assessment: The contract rejects embedding the finished full-tree digest inside that same finished tree. It separates a precisely defined base/excluded-property digest from the final serialized-tree hash kept in an external receipt. Canonicalization/exclusion rules remain a future independently reviewed implementation obligation, not an implemented handoff.

checks.point: Saved policy is historical and the old result remains7/10 and PHY_NOT_READY
checks.assessment: The contract preserves the original failed aggregate and source-consistent guarded observation, explicitly forbids replay onto another boot, and requires fresh same-boot/source/setup bindings. This direction supplies no evidence that an allocator, port, mapping, DMA or firmware is ready.

evidence.source_fact: Recorded STOP preserves7/10, PHY_NOT_READY, no new boot/init/retry, compiled-out shared writers and GPU hold.

checks.assessment: The source/API feasibility observations are explicitly conditional. Defined kernel symbols are not compiled-reader ABI/import proof. No guest helper, native reader, allocator or handoff exists by virtue of this contract; admission remains blocked.

evidence.source_fact: PE_state exposes a void BootArgs pointer, not a validated per-revision decoder.
Loader-info API reads one named pair and narrows length to int; it is not an exhaustive reservation iterator.

saved_metadata_crosscheck.method: Read-only ephemeral decoding of already saved bytes using the pinned formats; no transport import, source/helper file, mutation or target operation. Only counts and predicates are retained here.
limits: No raw interval, device property, identifier or lab address is copied into this review.
Numeric remap comparison does not prove physical remap semantics.
These historical predicates establish no exclusion completeness or fresh-boot policy.

remaining_blockers: A trusted same-boot bounded exclusion-source coverage/validation set; the existing finite MCC list and known disjointness cannot manufacture completeness.
An independently reviewed base/excluded-property digest format, serializer/decoder and exact same-setup guest-copy-only binding; none is admitted by this report.
Source-bound common-prefix/per-revision BootArgs reader and actual native layout/import checks before use; sizeof(native boot_args) is not the capture format.
Current native allocation/protection/lifetime and hardware prerequisites remain separately gated; historical policy cannot authorize a fresh boot.
stop_boundary: Review report only. No allocator, runtime, guest handoff or hardware admission.
